name: Eliezer
overview: Eliezer is a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically for his role as a trumpeter. His identification with the Levitical tribe situates him within the priestly and musical functions of Israel's worship. Beyond his role as a trumpeter, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliezer means 'G-d is my help,' reflecting a reliance on divine assistance. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:24 and was not given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning consistent with his service in worship.
familyAndRelationships: Eliezer is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical lineage responsible for religious duties. Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Eliezer's significance lies in his role as a trumpeter within the Levitical service, contributing to the worship and ceremonial life of Israel. His presence in the biblical record highlights the importance of music and ritual in honoring God. As a Levite, his service exemplifies faithful participation in the worship practices ordained by God.
